name: Agilent BioTek EL406
status_line: In PyLabRobot, v1 class EL406, registry status mostly (docs/_static/devices.json:120-122). Binary frames over FTDI USB.
reaches: FTDI USB, 38400 baud 8N2, no flow control. Host speaks first: 11-byte header (cmd, length, checksum), payload (pylabrobot/agilent/biotek/el406/protocol.py:15-25). Reply: ACK 0x06, header, data (pylabrobot/agilent/biotek/el406/el406.py:318-319). Steps polled by 0x92 (pylabrobot/agilent/biotek/el406/el406.py:595).
decoded_from: The v1 code names no source for the protocol. Legacy wash tests check bytes against reference captures from real EL406 hardware (pylabrobot/legacy/plate_washing/biotek/el406/steps_wash_tests.py:570-571). Some limits are labelled as the vendor GUI's (pylabrobot/agilent/biotek/el406/peristaltic_dispenser.py:176 and pylabrobot/agilent/biotek/el406/el406.py:1015-1018).
steps: Connect the EL406 by USB. setup() opens it as an FTDI device at 38400 baud 8N2, no flow control (pylabrobot/agilent/biotek/el406/el406.py:147-157).
Create EL406(name="el406", device_id=<FTDI serial>); the FTDI layer refuses to pick when several devices match (pylabrobot/io/ftdi.py:601-606 and pylabrobot/agilent/biotek/el406/el406.py:84).

await el406.setup(): it sends TEST_COMM 0x73, INIT_STATE 0xA0, then a full RESET 0x70 unless skip_reset=True (pylabrobot/agilent/biotek/el406/el406.py:178-186 and pylabrobot/agilent/biotek/el406/el406.py:290-303).
el406.set_plate(plate) with the PLR plate really loaded: 96, 384 or 1536 wells only (pylabrobot/agilent/biotek/el406/el406.py:113-119 and pylabrobot/agilent/biotek/el406/helpers.py:67-74).

In async with el406.batch(): peristaltic_dispenser.prime(volume=...), .dispense(volumes={col: uL}) (pylabrobot/agilent/biotek/el406/peristaltic_dispenser.py:83-94 and pylabrobot/agilent/biotek/el406/peristaltic_dispenser.py:139-145).
await el406.stop(). Check the wells by eye and file the upstream device test report (docs/user_guide/needs-testing.md:31-35).
scenario: Seed cells into a 384-well plate: set up, open a batch, prime the peristaltic lines with 500 uL, dispense 40 uL into every well (24 columns), close the batch. Made-up round volumes.
real: Upstream EL406 class and its peristaltic dispenser, unchanged
Every frame byte the driver writes, incl. the 0x8F dispense frame
Error code table and message for 0x1355
simulated: The EL406: frame and checksum decoding, replies, poll states
Device state: plate type, prime volume, uL per column, steps
Faults: dropped dispense reply; error 0x1355 in place of the dispense
not_checked: Any physical EL406; nothing here ran on hardware
Real reply header bytes beyond length and command echo (TODO_1)
Real busy time and post-fault state of a step (TODO_2)
limits: No tests for the v1 class: pylabrobot/agilent/biotek/el406/ has no *_tests.py; wire tests are legacy only, with a canned MockFTDI (pylabrobot/legacy/plate_washing/biotek/el406/mock_tests.py:72).
Replies are not checked: the driver reads only the length at header bytes 7-8 and ignores markers and checksum (pylabrobot/agilent/biotek/el406/el406.py:364-371).
batch() first sends 7 unnamed commands (0xBF ... 0x010A) and only logs a warning if they fail (pylabrobot/agilent/biotek/el406/el406.py:724-731).

Docstrings say the plate comes from the plate_holder (pylabrobot/agilent/biotek/el406/el406.py:682 and pylabrobot/agilent/biotek/el406/el406.py:1021), but only set_plate() sets it (pylabrobot/agilent/biotek/el406/el406.py:113-119).
